## (1) Andy Prevalsky — Background Findings

**Identity/Location:** Full name Andy Prevalsky, personal email andyprevalsky@yahoo.com (legacy) plus andy@roselabs.ai / andyprevalsky111@gmail.com. Grew up in Coppell, TX (Dallas–Fort Worth area, Coppell ISD school emails, 972 area code family contacts). Family/mom still reachable at a 972 (Dallas) number. Later data (2026) shows him ordering coffee at the Ferry Building in San Francisco, suggesting current SF Bay Area residence — consistent with a "Dallas roots, now SF-based tech" profile. [1][2]

**High school:** Attended Coppell High School through 10th grade, then was admitted to and attended the **Texas Academy of Mathematics and Science (TAMS)** — a selective early-college-entrance residential program at the University of North Texas (UNT) for TX students who complete grades 11–12 while simultaneously earning UNT college credit. He was "TAMS Class of 2017," got in around April 2015, and did a research internship/scholarship in Professor Rodney Nielsen's HiLT (human-computer interaction/ML/NLP) lab at UNT in 2016, including a UNT computer-science research credit and coding experience (Java, HTML, AJAX). He also competed in HOSA (Health Occupations Students of America) medical-society events. [1][3][4]

**College acceptance/attendance:** Because TAMS is a UNT-embedded early-college program, he was concurrently a UNT student (UNT emails: AndyPrevalsky@my.unt.edu, course evaluations for MATH 1650, biology courses, etc., 2015–2016) and earned some college credit while in the program. In Dec 2016 he was offered a full-ride **UT Dallas Academic Excellence Scholarship (Honors level)** for Fall 2017 entry (covering tuition, $3,000/semester stipend) — it's unclear from available data whether he accepted/matriculated at UT Dallas. He was also actively doing "college apps" in Nov–Dec 2016 (essays reference a "local university" research project, likely the UNT HiLT lab). No records after 2016 confirm a bachelor's degree completion — consistent with the premise that he does not currently hold an undergraduate degree. [1][3]

**Skills/Achievements relevant to a Stanford transfer application:**
- Strong STEM/CS aptitude from an early age (built his own PC, taught himself scripting/automation as a kid).
- Selected into TAMS, a highly competitive Texas early-college STEM program (comparable rigor to strong high-school + some college coursework).
- Academic Excellence Scholarship (Honors) offer from UT Dallas — signals strong academic record/GPA in high school/TAMS.
- Hands-on CS research experience at a university lab (HCI, ML, NLP) under a professor, including real coding work (Java/HTML/AJAX).
- Extracurriculars: HOSA medical society competitor, basketball, community service interest.
- Current professional signal: contact/domain evidence (andy@roselabs.ai, "Rose Labs architecture notes" in his Claude documents, an agent platform "roselabs.ai" actively used for daily-life AI agent tasks) strongly suggests he is a **founder/builder at a startup called Rose Labs** (roselabs.ai), fitting the "YC fam" / startup-founder profile referenced in his contacts. This is inferred from document/domain evidence, not an explicit LinkedIn/bio confirmation — I could not directly access a LinkedIn profile or an explicit "founder" title/bio text in the data available.

**Gaps:** No explicit LinkedIn profile, no confirmation of current job title, no confirmation of whether he ever formally enrolled/withdrew from UT Dallas or another four-year college, no current GPA/transcript data, no age (likely mid-20s given 2016 HS timeline — TAMS class of 2017 implies birth ~1999, so he'd be ~26-27 in 2026), no explicit "YC" (Y Combinator) confirmation beyond the contact-list label mentioned in the task prompt (not independently found in searched data).

## (2) Stanford Undergraduate Transfer Admission — Requirements & Strategy (for someone without a completed bachelor's degree)

Note: Live web research on Stanford's official 2026–2027 transfer requirements was not completed within this session (tool budget exhausted); below reflects standard, well-established Stanford transfer policy that has been stable for recent cycles — verify exact current-cycle dates on admission.stanford.edu before applying.

- **Eligibility:** Stanford accepts transfer applicants who have completed at least one full year (two semesters/three quarters) of full-time college coursework by the time of matriculation, and have NOT yet earned a bachelor's degree — a good structural fit for Andy given he has some UNT/TAMS college credit but no BA.
- **Application deadline:** Transfer applications typically due **March 15** (for fall matriculation), via the Coalition Application or Common App with the Stanford-specific supplement; decisions released in mid-May.
- **Components:** Common App/Coalition App, Stanford Transfer supplement essays (several short essays on intellectual curiosity, community, "why Stanford"), official transcripts from ALL post-secondary institutions attended, a college report/dean's certification form, one or two academic letters of recommendation from college instructors, standardized testing (Stanford has been test-optional in recent cycles — confirm current policy), and a $90 application fee (or fee waiver).
- **Academic bar:** No official minimum GPA is published, but admitted transfers typically show strong (~3.7+) college GPA, rigorous coursework (especially in intended major), and demonstrated intellectual vitality/leadership since high school.
- **Acceptance rate:** Extremely low — historically under 2% (about 1–2%), admitting only a small transfer cohort (historically ~15-30 students/year), making it one of the most selective transfer pathways in the US.
- **Strategy fit for Andy:** Given his profile (TAMS/UNT early-college STEM credit, HiLT research lab experience, strong HS academic record/scholarship offers, and — if confirmed — startup-founder experience via Rose Labs/YC ecosystem), a competitive Stanford transfer application would need to: (a) complete/solidify a strong recent college GPA (e.g., via community college or UNT/UT Dallas coursework, ideally 1+ full year), (b) leverage startup/founder accomplishments (product traction, YC affiliation, technical work) as evidence of intellectual vitality and initiative — Stanford transfer essays value exactly this kind of demonstrated impact, (c) secure strong letters from college instructors and possibly a professional/founder reference, (d) frame the "gap" between TAMS/UNT and now as a coherent narrative of entrepreneurial/technical growth. Given the sub-2% admit rate, alternative or parallel plans (other selective transfer targets, or credential paths like Stanford's non-degree/exec-ed programs, or waiting for stronger achievements) should be considered as a hedge.
